long_biography.plain_text:
Margulies entered the industry as a financial analyst for broker John Cushman, then supervised a Northern California office development while studying at UCLA. He later enlarged JMB Realty's special-projects portfolio before becoming Apollo Real Estate Partners' West Coast representative in 1997. That sequence gave him experience in development, joint ventures and institutional capital across several western markets.

In 2002, Margulies and Arnold Rosenstein established their own Beverly Hills firm. Its strategy emphasized underused or difficult sites whose value could be improved through acquisition, financing, construction oversight and repositioning. Related New Pacific entities broadened the platform into private equity and early-stage companies. The result was a founder-led model that combined institutional investment methods with direct control of development and asset management.
